title: Notice of Removal – Civil Action No. 24-0372
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
DALLAS DIVISION

ALICIA R. MARTINEZ,                     )
     Plaintiff,                         )
                                         )
v.                                       )  Docket No. 3:24-cv-0372
                                         )
BRYANT LAW FIRM AND                      )
DEBORAH BRYANT,                          )
     Defendants.                         )

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that Defendants, Bryant Law Firm and Deborah Bryant, hereby remove the above-captioned action from the 160th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, to this Court pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a). This action is one over which this Court has original jurisdiction because it arises under the laws of the United States, specifically the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq., and the parties are citizens of different states.

1. The original petition was filed on January 12, 2024, in the 160th District Court, Dallas County, Texas, assigned Cause No. DC-24-00123.

2. Plaintiff Alicia R. Martinez resides in Dallas County, Texas. Defendant Bryant Law Firm is a Texas professional corporation with its principal place of business at 1200 Commerce Street, Dallas, Texas 75202. Defendant Deborah Bryant is an individual resident of Dallas County, Texas.

3. The amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs, as Plaintiff seeks compensatory and punitive damages for alleged violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

4. Removal is timely filed within 30 days of service of the original petition. Service was effected on Defendants on February 10, 2024.

5. A copy of all pleadings, orders, and other papers filed in the state court action is attached hereto as Exhibit A, Bates numbered BRYANT0001–BRYANT0045.

6. Defendants rely on the affidavit of John P. O’Neil, Jr., attached as Exhibit B, in support of the diversity jurisdiction.

7. The following individuals are known to have an interest in this proceeding: Plaintiff Alicia R. Martinez, Defendant Deborah Bryant, counsel for Plaintiff Thomas M. Gallagher (Bar No. 24012345), and counsel for Defendants Sarah K. Lin (Bar No. 24067890).

8. In her deposition, Plaintiff stated that she had a telephone conversation on March 15, 2023, with a representative of the firm, during which her Social Security number, 456-78-9012, was discussed. She also provided her email address, alicia.martinez@email.com, and her phone number, (214) 555-0199.

9. Plaintiff’s date of birth is May 14, 1980, as reflected in the records produced.

10. The vehicle involved in the underlying credit dispute is a 2021 Toyota Camry, VIN 4T1B11HK1MU123456, insured under Policy No. POL-9876543.

11. During the state court proceedings, the Honorable Linda S. Rothstein presided. The case was originally assigned to Judge Rothstein.

12. As the United States Supreme Court noted in 

Hertz Corp. v. Friend, 559 U.S. 77 (2010), the principal place of business is the “nerve center.” See also 

Merrill Lynch v. Dabit, 547 U.S. 71 (2006).

13. The removal is proper under the language of 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b), as no prior removal has occurred.

WHEREFORE, Defendants respectfully request that this Court accept jurisdiction and proceed accordingly.

Dated: February 28, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Sarah K. Lin
Sarah K. Lin
Attorney for Defendants
Lin & Associates, PLLC
300 Main Street, Suite 500
Dallas, TX 75201
(214) 555-0178
sarah.lin@linassociates.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I hereby certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing Notice of Removal was served on counsel for Plaintiff, Thomas M. Gallagher, on February 28, 2024, via ECF.

/s/ Sarah K. Lin

title: Notice of Removal – Civil Action No. 24-0981
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
TEXARKANA DIVISION

GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN, INC.,               )
     Plaintiff,                         )
                                         )
v.                                       )  Docket No. 5:24-cv-0981
                                         )
WILCOX & WILCOX, LLC,                    )
     Defendant.                          )

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Defendant Wilcox & Wilcox, LLC, by and through its undersigned counsel, removes this civil action from the 202nd Judicial District Court of Bowie County, Texas, to the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas, Texarkana Division. This removal is based on diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a).

1. The state court action was filed on March 1, 2024, in Cause No. 24-00987-B, with the Honorable Patricia A. Nguyen presiding.

2. Plaintiff Global Supply Chain, Inc. is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in Wilmington, Delaware. Defendant Wilcox & Wilcox, LLC is a Texas limited liability company with its principal place of business in Texarkana, Texas.

3. The matter in controversy exceeds the sum of $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs. Plaintiff seeks damages for breach of contract and fraud in the amount of $250,000.

4. Removal is timely as the complaint was served on Defendant on March 5, 2024, and this notice is filed within 30 days.

5. Attached as Exhibit A (Bates stamped WILCOX0001–WILCOX0020) is a copy of the state court petition and all orders entered.

6. In the petition, Plaintiff alleges that a representative of Defendant, one James T. Henderson, made false representations. Mr. Henderson’s bar number is 24123456.

7. During a deposition, the deponent referred to exhibitJohn Doe, a document that was not properly marked. The witness testified that “[Smith] was the person who signed the contract.” The witness also identified a phone number, (903) 555-0182, and an email, james.henderson@wilcoxlaw.com.

8. Defendant’s insurance policy number is INS-5544332, and the vehicle used in the transaction has VIN 2GCEC13T5Y1234543.

9. Plaintiff’s corporate representative, Michael O’Brien, provided his date of birth as July 22, 1975, during discovery.

10. The Social Security number of a non-party witness, 123-45-6789, was inadvertently disclosed in a document produced.

11. The court in 

Johnson v. MGM/UA, 200 F.3d 345 (5th Cir. 2000) held that the forum defendant rule does not bar removal. See also 

Caterpillar Inc. v. Lewis, 519 U.S. 61 (1996).

12. The removal is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a) because the parties are completely diverse and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

WHEREFORE, Defendant requests that this Court accept removal and proceed.

Dated: March 15, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Michael T. O’Brien
Michael T. O’Brien
Attorney for Defendant
O’Brien & Associates
100 Federal Street, Texarkana, TX 75501
(903) 555-0172
m.obrien@obrienlaw.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a copy of this Notice was served on counsel for Plaintiff, Rebecca L. Torres, on March 15, 2024.

/s/ Michael T. O’Brien

title: Notice of Removal – Civil Action No. 24-1573
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

PATRICIA L. CHEN,                        )
     Plaintiff,                         )
                                         )
v.                                       )  Docket No. 4:24-cv-1573
                                         )
HARRIS COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT,         )
     Defendant.                          )

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

Defendant Harris County Hospital District (the “District”) removes this action from the 333rd Judicial District Court of Harris County, Texas, to this Court. The action arises under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act (EMTALA), 42 U.S.C. § 1395dd, and thus federal question jurisdiction exists.

1. The state court petition was filed on April 5, 2024, assigned Cause No. 2024-12345, before Judge David H. McAllister.

2. Plaintiff Patricia L. Chen is a resident of Houston, Harris County, Texas. Defendant Harris County Hospital District is a political subdivision of the State of Texas with its principal office at 2525 Holly Hall Street, Houston, TX 77054.

3. The action challenges the District’s failure to provide appropriate medical screening as required by EMTALA.

4. Plaintiff’s counsel is Robert “Bob” A. Nguyen, Bar No. 24098765. Defendant is represented by Carolyn S. Barnes, Bar No. 24109876.

5. In her complaint, Plaintiff alleges she was denied treatment on April 1, 2024. She provided her phone number, (713) 555-0143, and email, patricia.chen@email.net. Her date of birth is November 3, 1988.

6. A document produced by the District contains Plaintiff’s Social Security number, 987-65-4321, and policy number MED-1122334.

7. The vehicle Plaintiff was transported in bears VIN 5XYZG3AB4DG123456.

8. During a telephonic conference, Judge McAllister referred to the testimony of “[Chen],” which appears on page 7 of the transcript.

9. The District’s emergency room records are Bates stamped HCHD0001–HCHD0150.

10. The removal is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a) and 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b). There is no prior removal.

11. The case of 

Roberts v. Galen of Virginia, 525 U.S. 249 (1999) interprets EMTALA. See also 

Summers v. Baptist Medical Center, 91 F.3d 1132 (8th Cir. 1996).

12. The District also relies on the declaration of Dr. Evelyn O’Neil-Scott, attached as Exhibit B.

WHEREFORE, Defendant respectfully requests that this Court accept removal.

Dated: April 20, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Carolyn S. Barnes
Carolyn S. Barnes
Attorney for Defendant
Barnes & Thompson, LLP
1000 Louisiana Street, Suite 300
Houston, TX 77002
(713) 555-0117
carolyn.barnes@barnes-law.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that the foregoing was served on Robert A. Nguyen on April 20, 2024.

/s/ Carolyn S. Barnes
public_law: Roberts v. Galen of Virginia, 525 U.S. 249 (1999)
Summers v. Baptist Medical Center, 91 F.3d 1132 (8th Cir. 1996)

title: Notice of Removal – Civil Action No. 24-2114
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE WESTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
AUSTIN DIVISION

FINLEY R. HAYES,                         )
     Plaintiff,                         )
                                         )
v.                                       )  Docket No. 1:24-cv-2114
                                         )
TURNER CONSTRUCTION CO.,                 )
     Defendant.                          )

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

Defendant Turner Construction Co. removes this action from the 261st Judicial District Court of Travis County, Texas, to this Court. This Court has subject matter jurisdiction under the diversity statute, 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a), because the parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

1. The state court action was filed on May 10, 2024, in Cause No. D-1-GN-24-002345, before the Honorable Julia M. Park.

2. Plaintiff Finley R. Hayes is a citizen of California, residing in Los Angeles County. Defendant Turner Construction Co. is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business in Austin, Texas.

3. Plaintiff seeks damages exceeding $150,000 for personal injuries sustained at a construction site.

4. Plaintiff is represented by counsel, Amanda S. Torres, Bar No. 24011223. Defendant is represented by counsel, William J. Chen, Bar No. 24022334.

5. The incident report lists Plaintiff’s phone as (512) 555-0189 and email as finley.hayes@mail.com. His date of birth is December 9, 1992.

6. A medical record contains Plaintiff’s Social Security number, 321-54-8765, and insurance policy number PL-4455667.

7. The construction vehicle involved has VIN 1FDKF37G4XEB12345.

8. In a deposition, the witness stated that “[Hayes] was operating the forklift.” The transcript also erroneously includes “exhibitJohn Doe” as a placeholder.

9. Discovery materials are Bates stamped TURNER0001–TURNER0099.

10. The removal is timely under 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b). No prior removal has been sought.

11. The applicable law includes § 17.50 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code, which governs deceptive trade practices.

12. The court in 

Bridgestone/Firestone v. Gandy, 143 S.W.3d 209 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2004, pet. denied) addressed similar issues. See also 

Ford Motor Co. v. Miles, 141 S.W.3d 444 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2004, no pet.).

WHEREFORE, Defendant requests that this Court accept removal.

Dated: June 1, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ William J. Chen
William J. Chen
Attorney for Defendant
Chen & Associates, PLLC
500 Congress Avenue, Suite 200
Austin, TX 78701
(512) 555-0121
william.chen@chenlaw.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a copy of this Notice was served on Amanda S. Torres on June 1, 2024.

/s/ William J. Chen

Bridgestone/Firestone v. Gandy, 143 S.W.3d 209 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2004, pet. denied)

title: Notice of Removal – Civil Action No. 24-2789
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

LISA M. O’NEIL,                         )

v.                                       )  Docket No. 4:24-cv-2789
                                         )
WESTERN TEXAS ENERGY CORP.,              )
     Defendant.                          )

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

Defendant Western Texas Energy Corp. removes this action from the 348th Judicial District Court of Tarrant County, Texas, to this Court. This removal is based on federal question jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1331, as Plaintiff’s claims arise under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, 42 U.S.C. § 6901 et seq.

1. The state court petition was filed on June 15, 2024, assigned Cause No. 348-123456-24, before Judge Anthony R. Davis.

2. Plaintiff Lisa M. O’Neil is a resident of Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas. Defendant Western Texas Energy Corp. is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business at 4500 Energy Lane, Fort Worth, TX 76102.

3. The action concerns alleged improper disposal of hazardous waste.

4. Plaintiff is represented by counsel, Jonathan S. Park, Bar No. 24033445. Defendant is represented by counsel, Emily R. Torres, Bar No. 24044556.

5. In her complaint, Plaintiff provides her phone, (817) 555-0167, and email, lisa.oneil@energywatch.org. Her date of birth is August 4, 1985.

6. A document produced by Defendant contains Plaintiff’s Social Security number, 654-32-1098, and a policy number ENV-7788990.

7. The company vehicle used in waste transport has VIN 1M2G40401GW123456.

8. During a hearing, Judge Davis said, “The testimony of [O’Neil] is crucial.” The transcript also contains a typographical error “exhibitJohn Doe”.

9. Discovery materials are Bates stamped WTE0001–WTE0075.

10. Removal is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a) and 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b). No previous removal exists.

11. The case of 

Meghrig v. KFC Western, Inc., 516 U.S. 479 (1996) interpreted RCRA. See also 

City of Chicago v. Environmental Defense Fund, 511 U.S. 328 (1994).

12. The relevant statute includes 42 U.S.C. § 6972, which provides for citizen suits.

WHEREFORE, Defendant respectfully requests that this Court accept removal.

Dated: July 1, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Emily R. Torres
Emily R. Torres
Attorney for Defendant
Torres Law Group
200 Main Street, Suite 400
Fort Worth, TX 76102
(817) 555-0135
emily.torres@torres-law.com

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that the foregoing was served on Jonathan S. Park on July 1, 2024.

/s/ Emily R. Torres

City of Chicago v. Environmental Defense Fund, 511 U.S. 328 (1994)
